narration.full_text: Namaste students! In this section, we will delve deeper into the algebraic method of solving linear equations, specifically focusing on the elimination method. We'll also tackle how to apply this powerful technique to solve real-world word problems, transforming everyday scenarios into mathematical models. Our goal is to master the elimination method for solving linear equations. We will also learn to solve complex word problems by setting up and solving equations using the elimination method. Finally, we will analyze real-world scenarios and translate them into mathematical models. Let's look at an example where the equations are multiples of each other. Consider the system: Equation 1 is 4x + 6y = 8, and Equation 2 is 2x + 3y = 4. Notice that if you multiply Equation 2 by 2, you get 4x + 6y = 8, which is identical to Equation 1. This means the two equations represent the exact same line. When two linear equations are essentially the same, they have infinitely many solutions. Every point on that line is a solution to both equations. This is a special case to watch out for when using the elimination method.
